Pretty useful stuff -- to pilots. In order to regulate aviation, they have an authority over "airspace" and most drone-space is Class G... so... they're kind of within their rights. I get that it's annoying, but when I consider what policies they've shot down that politicians have proposed, I think it's more okay. Bear with me. The FAA is supposed to support private pilots and commercial pilots. Airlines would love to eliminate private pilots. For one, they wouldn't have to share airport services. Right now, some guy in a tiny Tomahawk can land at Logan. To make an analogy, the airports now kind of hold to a system like net neutrality.
